## Big Question {.role-slide}

Can several linguistic measurements be represented by a smaller number of recurring numerical patterns?

## Data {.role-slide}

A vowel token may have F1, F2, F3, duration, and voice quality measurements.

A verb may have frequencies for more than one hundred syntactic frames.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

The columns may share structure, but a lower dimensional representation is meaningful only with respect to a declared matrix and reconstruction task.

## This Module {.role-slide .compact}

1. Define rows, columns, origins, and units.
2. Build one rank one pattern.
3. Order several patterns with the singular value decomposition.
4. Interpret scores, loadings, and reconstructed cells.
5. Select rank using held out reconstruction.
6. Test whether VALEX components predict MegaAcceptability profiles.

## Represent the measurements {.section-slide}

Rows, columns, origins, and units

## Question {.role-slide}

What does one cell of a linguistic data matrix measure?

## Answer {.role-slide}

For $\mathbf X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$,

$$x_{ij}=\text{the value of variable }j\text{ for object }i.$$

## Data {.role-slide}

| token | F1 | F2 | F3 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| token 1 | 500 | 1500 | 2200 |
| token 2 | 550 | 1450 | 2150 |
| token 3 | 300 | 2300 | 3000 |
| token 4 | 320 | 2250 | 2950 |

## Question {.role-slide}

What does $x_{31}=300$ mean?

## Answer {.role-slide}

Token 3 has an F1 measurement of 300 Hz.

Both indices are required for that interpretation.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

If rows are tokens, scores locate tokens. If rows are speakers, scores locate speakers.

Aggregation changes the represented object.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

Columns define the representation.

Including duration and twice duration gives the same measurement two coordinates.

## Method {.role-slide .compact}

Before factorization, record what one row represents, how rows were selected, what each column measures, which columns repeat information, and which collection the objects come from.

## Data {.role-slide}

PHOIBLE may contain several inventories for one language from different sources.

The row selection rule must be fixed before a language by segment matrix is interpreted.

<span class="source">PHOIBLE 2.0 documentation</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

PHOIBLE 2.0 download and citation page: https://phoible.org/download

PHOIBLE FAQ on multiple inventories and sources: https://phoible.org/faq
:::

## Question {.role-slide}

What coordinate system should later components use?

## Answer {.role-slide}

Centering changes a column's origin. Scaling changes its unit.

These operations recall the [earlier treatment of centering](../../regression-models/centering-predictors.html).

## Method {.role-slide}

$$x^c_{ij}=x_{ij}-\bar x_j$$

$$z_{ij}=\frac{x_{ij}-\bar x_j}{s_j}$$

## Question {.role-slide}

Durations are 100, 120, and 140 ms.

What are their standardized values?

## Answer {.role-slide}

The mean is 120 ms and the sample standard deviation is 20 ms.

The standardized values are $-1$, $0$, and $1$.

## Important Point #3 {.role-slide}

Giving every column variance one is a weighting decision.

It is not a neutral software default.

## Important Point #4 {.role-slide}

New observations must use the training means and standard deviations.

Recomputing them on evaluation observations creates [data leakage](../../model-criticism-and-prediction/training-and-test-data.html#leakage).

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Factorization reorganizes the information supplied in a matrix. It cannot recover omitted observations or repair a theoretically inappropriate representation.

## Build component patterns {.section-slide}

From one outer product to an ordered decomposition

## Question {.role-slide}

When can one pattern reproduce every cell of a matrix?

## Answer {.role-slide}

A nonzero matrix has [rank one](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html) when it can be written as an outer product:

$$\mathbf X=\mathbf a\mathbf b^{\mathsf T}.$$

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 7: https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html
:::

## Data {.role-slide}

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}2&4\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\4&8\\6&12\end{bmatrix}.
$$

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

The first vector varies across rows. The second gives the column pattern.

All rows and columns are proportional.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

Rank is an algebraic property of the matrix.

It is not a psychological construct or a linguistic category.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

Most linguistic matrices are not exactly rank one.

We need an ordered set of approximate rank one patterns.

## Answer {.role-slide}

The [singular value decomposition](https://cs357.cs.illinois.edu/textbook/notes/svd.html), or SVD, writes

$$\mathbf X=\mathbf U\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}.$$

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

University of Illinois CS 357, Singular Value Decomposition: https://cs357.cs.illinois.edu/textbook/notes/svd.html
:::

## Answer {.role-slide}

The columns of $\mathbf U$ are [left singular vectors](https://cs357.cs.illinois.edu/textbook/notes/svd.html).

The columns of $\mathbf V$ are [right singular vectors](https://cs357.cs.illinois.edu/textbook/notes/svd.html).

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

University of Illinois CS 357, Singular Value Decomposition: https://cs357.cs.illinois.edu/textbook/notes/svd.html
:::

## Output {.role-slide}

$$\mathbf X=\sum_{k=1}^r\sigma_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T},\qquad \sigma_1\geq\sigma_2\geq\cdots>0.$$

Each term is rank one.

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

The singular value $\sigma_k$ measures the strength of term $k$ under squared reconstruction error.

The first term is the closest rank one approximation.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

Singular vectors have arbitrary sign.

Replacing $\mathbf u_k$ and $\mathbf v_k$ by their negatives leaves the reconstructed matrix unchanged.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Palarea Albaladejo, Principal Components Analysis, sign indeterminacy: https://imae.udg.edu/~jpalarea/StatsDS/principal-components-analysis.html
:::

## Important Point #3 {.role-slide}

Repeated singular values weaken interpretation of individual directions.

The associated subspace is identified more strongly than one orientation within it.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

The SVD orders rank one patterns by their contribution to squared reconstruction of the specified matrix.

## Principal components {.section-slide}

Directions of variation around column means

## Question {.role-slide}

Which direction through the measured variables has the greatest projected variation?

## Answer {.role-slide}

[Principal component analysis](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html), or PCA, finds orthogonal directions in a centered matrix, ordered by projected variance.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 7: https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html
:::

## Method {.role-slide}

Center the columns, then decompose

$$\mathbf X_c=\mathbf U\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}.$$

## Answer {.role-slide}

The columns of $\mathbf V$ are the [principal component directions](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html).

The [score matrix](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html) is

$$\mathbf Z=\mathbf X_c\mathbf V=\mathbf U\boldsymbol\Sigma.$$

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 7: https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html
:::

## Goal {.role-slide}

The first direction $\mathbf v_1$ maximizes

$$\operatorname{Var}(\mathbf X_c\mathbf v)$$

subject to $\lVert\mathbf v\rVert_2=1$.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

PCA uses numerical variation in the matrix.

It does not use category labels or a theory of the response unless they were built into the representation.

## Question {.role-slide}

If F1 and F2 both increase together across tokens, should the first direction assign them the same sign or opposite signs?

## Answer {.role-slide}

The same sign represents their common increase.

The complete direction may be multiplied by $-1$ without changing the component.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

PCA identifies directions that reconstruct centered numerical variation. A direction does not acquire a linguistic interpretation from its rank alone.

## Read and reconstruct components {.section-slide}

Row coordinates, variable directions, and residual cells

## Question {.role-slide}

Which quantity locates an observation, and which quantity describes a component direction through variables?

## Answer {.role-slide}

[Scores](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html) locate row observations.

[Loadings](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html) are the entries of unit length component directions through the original variables.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 7: https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html
:::

## Method {.role-slide}

For centered row $\mathbf x_i^c$ and component direction $\mathbf v_k$,

$$z_{ik}=\mathbf x_i^{c\mathsf T}\mathbf v_k.$$

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

Join scores to linguistic metadata by stable row identifiers.

Row order alone is fragile after filtering or reshaping.

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

Read a loading pattern across variables and a score pattern across observations.

Do not interpret one isolated sign without its companion entries and metadata.

## Question {.role-slide}

What does retaining the first $K$ components reproduce?

## Answer {.role-slide}

A [rank-$K$ approximation](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html) is

$$\widehat{\mathbf X}_K=\sum_{k=1}^K\sigma_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}.$$

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 7: https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html
:::

## Output {.role-slide}

The residual matrix is

$$\mathbf E_K=\mathbf X-\widehat{\mathbf X}_K.$$

Every cell records what the retained terms did not reconstruct.

## Answer {.role-slide}

For centered data, the [proportion of variance explained](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html) is

$$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^K\sigma_k^2}{\sum_{k=1}^r\sigma_k^2}.$$

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 7: https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson07.html
:::

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

Observed variance explained is an in sample reconstruction summary.

It is not held out prediction and not a measure of linguistic information.

## Question {.role-slide}

How are reconstructed standardized values returned to the original units?

## Answer {.role-slide}

Multiply each column by its training standard deviation, then add its training mean.

The inverse transformation must use the fitted coordinate system.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Scores and loadings interpret the low rank coordinates. Reconstruction returns those coordinates to the cells that defined the original linguistic representation.

## Choose the retained rank {.section-slide}

Separate fitting, selection, and final evaluation

## Question {.role-slide}

How many components should be retained for a declared reconstruction task?

## Approach {.role-slide}

Choose the rank that minimizes reconstruction loss on validation cells that did not determine the components.

## Implementation {.role-slide .compact}

1. Fit preprocessing and components on training data.
2. Evaluate fixed candidate ranks on validation data.
3. Select one rank using the declared loss.
4. Refit on training plus validation data.
5. Evaluate once on untouched test data.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

Centering, scaling, imputation, and component directions are fitted operations.

Each must remain inside the training split.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

Observed reconstruction error decreases whenever rank increases.

It therefore cannot choose rank without an external criterion.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

A bend in a scree plot describes the singular value sequence.

It does not directly answer which rank predicts held out cells best.

## Important Point #3 {.role-slide}

Cell weighting defines the evaluation target.

Equal cell, row, and variable weighting answer different reconstruction questions.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

A selected rank is conditional on the representation, split, candidate set, and loss. It is not the true number of linguistic dimensions.

## Corpus distributions and clause selection {.section-slide}

VALEX predictors and MegaAcceptability profiles

## Question {.role-slide}

Can a verb's corpus distribution predict its acceptability across clause embedding frames?

## Answer {.role-slide}

A verb's [selectional profile](https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001) records its acceptability across syntactic frames.

<span class="source">White and Rawlins 2020</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

White and Rawlins, Frequency, acceptability, and selection: https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001
:::

## Data {.role-slide}

MegaAcceptability supplies 50 frame judgments for each retained verb.

VALEX supplies a 109 dimensional corpus frame distribution for the same verb.

<span class="source">White and Rawlins 2020</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

White and Rawlins, Frequency, acceptability, and selection: https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001
:::

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

VALEX counts are converted to within verb proportions.

The predictor represents allocation across complement frames, not total verb frequency.

## Goal {.role-slide}

Compare two theoretically distinct predictors for verbs excluded from fitting.

The direct predictor uses all VALEX frame proportions. The factor predictor uses retained PCA scores.

## Method {.role-slide}

Both analyses use ridge regression to predict the same 50 response columns.

Only the predictor representation changes.

## Implementation {.role-slide .compact}

Outer grouped cross validation excludes complete verbs. Inner validation fits normalization, PCA, rank selection, and the ridge penalty using only the outer training verbs.

## Question {.role-slide}

May PCA be fitted once using all VALEX verbs because it does not use acceptability judgments?

## Answer {.role-slide}

No. The question concerns a new verb. Its VALEX row must not determine the component directions used to represent it.

## Output {.role-slide}

Out of sample $R^2$ compares each model with frame mean predictions fitted on the training verbs.

Positive values remove some baseline squared error.

## Result #1 {.role-slide}

The direct VALEX profile obtains out of sample $R^2=.246$ with a verb bootstrap interval of $[.224,.266]$.

<span class="source">Course analysis of White and Rawlins data</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course notes, VALEX and MegaAcceptability analysis: ../../factorization/valex-megaacceptability.html

White and Rawlins 2020: https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001
:::

## Result #2 {.role-slide}

The selected factor model obtains $R^2=.239$.

Factor minus direct is $-.0066$ with interval $[-.0100,-.0029]$.

<span class="source">Course analysis of White and Rawlins data</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course notes, VALEX and MegaAcceptability analysis: ../../factorization/valex-megaacceptability.html
:::

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

PCA compression does not improve this mapping.

Inner validation selects the largest candidate rank, 50, in every outer fold.

## Result #3 {.role-slide}

Prediction is weakest for object plus finite clause frames.

Direct $R^2$ is .083 there, compared with .254 for matched finite clauses without an object.

<span class="source">Course analysis of White and Rawlins data</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course notes, VALEX and MegaAcceptability analysis: ../../factorization/valex-megaacceptability.html

White and Rawlins 2020: https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.1001
:::

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Corpus distributions predict new verbs, but PCA directions of corpus variation discard a small amount of predictive information and do not repair the object frame failure.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

The result rejects this predictive compression.

It does not show that clause selection lacks abstract syntactic or semantic structure.

## Conclusion {.section-slide}

What a component can establish

## Big Question {.role-slide}

Can several linguistic measurements be represented by a smaller number of recurring numerical patterns?

## Answer {.role-slide .compact}

1. The matrix fixes the represented objects and measurements.
2. The coordinate system determines which variations count as large.
3. SVD orders rank one reconstruction patterns.
4. PCA applies that ordering to centered variation.
5. Scores, loadings, and reconstructions answer different questions.
6. Held out loss selects rank for a declared task.

## Question {.role-slide}

Which rows, columns, preprocessing choices, and evaluation loss license the proposed linguistic interpretation of a component?
